dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Hello. What’s your name?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: My name is Lee.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Jo?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: No. Lee.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Lee. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.text: Listen. My name is Jo. Write Jo.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Again, please.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.text: Write Jo.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Kim?

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.text: No. Jo.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Jo. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.text: Yes. Stop.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: What’s your name?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: Leo. L, E, O.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Code two, zero, nine?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: No. Two, zero, eight.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: I’m from Canada. I’m in Natal.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Is this your bag, Jo?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: No. My pen.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: This pen?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Two books?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: No. Three books.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: One coffee, please.

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.text: Tea?

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: No. Coffee, please.

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.text: Four credits.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Four?

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: English on Monday. At eleven, not ten. Room four.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Again, please.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Monday. At eleven. Room four.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Monday, at eleven, room four.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Is Ben a teacher?

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: No, he isn’t. He is a driver. Jo is a teacher.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Is Jo your neighbour?

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: No. Jo is my partner. Ben is my neighbour.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: And your job?

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: I’m a nurse.

dialogue.speaker: Paulo
dialogue.text: Do you work on Friday, Nina?

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: No, I don’t. What time do you study English?

dialogue.speaker: Paulo
dialogue.text: At nine in the morning. I’m free at noon.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: A conversation at noon?

dialogue.speaker: Paulo
dialogue.text: Yes. At the library?

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Yes. Friday, at noon, at the library.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Is there a bookshop near the flat?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Yes. The bookshop is opposite the library.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: At A?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: No. A is the library. The bookshop is at D.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: And our conversation?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: At the café, B, next to the library.

dialogue.speaker: Shop assistant
dialogue.text: How many eggs?

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Two eggs, please. And one bottle of milk.

dialogue.speaker: Shop assistant
dialogue.text: Four eggs?

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: No. Two. We have four eggs at home.

dialogue.speaker: Shop assistant
dialogue.text: Two eggs and one bottle of milk. Seven credits.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Seven?

dialogue.speaker: Shop assistant
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: Caller
dialogue.text: Are you working at the café, Jo?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: No. I’m at home. I’m studying now.

dialogue.speaker: Caller
dialogue.text: Is Kim studying too?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: No. Kim is cooking.

dialogue.speaker: Caller
dialogue.text: These blue books near you?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Yes. These are my books. Those red bags are not mine.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Would you like to join us on Friday?

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Sorry, I can’t come on Friday. I work in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Are you free on Saturday at nine?

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Yes. Is the event free?

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Yes. Bring water. Don’t take photos inside the library.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Saturday at nine. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Were you at the library yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: Yes, at nine. But it was closed.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Did you go home?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: No, we didn’t. We went to the café.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Did you see Kim?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: No. We saw Jo. Kim wasn’t there.

dialogue.speaker: Eva
dialogue.text: Did you watch a film?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: Yes, we did.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Are you going to bring the map, Rui?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: No. Kim is going to bring the map. I’m going to bring water.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: And the books?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: They’re in Kim’s bag.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Are we going to buy books?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: No. We’re going to read at the library.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: At ten?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Yes, at ten in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Is Room B still available from two to four on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes. There are eight seats.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Is twenty-eight credits the total fee?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes, for the whole room for two hours.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: And it’s at street level?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: We’d like Room B, please.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: I’ll send the confirmation. Please check it when it arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.text: Could you tell me where platform six is?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Next to platform five. Your train leaves at two forty.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.text: Thank you. I’ll call Jo now.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.text: The train arrives at three twenty. Can we meet at three thirty?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Yes. Outside the main entrance. If it rains, we’ll meet at the station café.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.text: Three thirty. If it rains, the café. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Is the blue bag with the white strip yours?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: No. Mine has a red strip.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: The one that has two books inside?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: Yes, and a silver bottle.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: What were you doing when the bus arrived?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: I was talking on the phone.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: The person who found your bag left it here. You can collect it after three.

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: Thank you. I’ll come at four.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Have you confirmed the room yet?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Yes. We’ve just confirmed Room B for Saturday, from two to four.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Is the total fee twenty-eight credits?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Yes. I’ve already sent the confirmation by email.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: I haven’t received it yet. Could you check the address?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Of course. Please use the fictional address on your form.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Thank you. I’ll check again.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Could you move my appointment to Tuesday at two?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Two isn’t available. We can offer three.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Three is fine. Could I use my own vocabulary card?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Please use the centre’s card during the practice. You mustn’t use a card during the separate observation.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Do I have to bring a notebook?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: No, you don’t have to. It’s optional.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: And a short break?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes, between the activities.

dialogue.speaker: Support
dialogue.text: Is the microphone on?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Yes. Should I turn off it now?

dialogue.speaker: Support
dialogue.text: Turn it off after the recording. Then look for the file in the practice folder.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: I found it. Is it shared automatically?

dialogue.speaker: Support
dialogue.text: No. It is checked by the teacher first.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: I’ll check the name carefully before I upload it.

dialogue.speaker: Support
dialogue.text: Good. You don’t need to send us a password.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Did you use to sing alone, Mara?

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: No, I didn’t. I used to sing with a choir on Fridays.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Do you still sing on Fridays?

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: No. Now I sing with a group on Sundays.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Did the rain stop the performance?

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: No. Although it rained, we performed indoors.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: What happened after the songs?

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: We talked to the audience and put the chairs away.

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: Have you finished checking the five descriptions?

dialogue.speaker: Writer
dialogue.text: Not yet. I’ve been checking them since Monday. I’ve finished three checks, but two still need work.

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: Does that mean three texts have been reviewed by another reader?

dialogue.speaker: Writer
dialogue.text: No. Those are my language checks. Only two have had another reader’s feedback.

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: When did you correct the wrong date?

dialogue.speaker: Writer
dialogue.text: Last Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: Can we announce the guide today?

dialogue.speaker: Writer
dialogue.text: I’d wait. We haven’t made the final recordings, and we still need to agree on responsibility for them.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Had the caretaker left before you arrived?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yes. We arrived at six, and he had left at five forty-five.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Could you contact him?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: At first, no. Then Mina found the number, and we managed to reach him at six twenty.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Did your group use to collect a key every Friday?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No. We used to have our own key. We would arrive early and set up the chairs.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Who failed to pass on the message?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I can’t identify that from what I know.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Have they confirmed the guide?

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Not yet. I’ll call them now.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: I’d rather postpone than replace the visit with a walk.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: I understand. We won’t treat the walk as agreed.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: And the deposit?

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: We won’t pay unless they confirm the guide and the price.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: When will you update us?

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: As soon as I receive their reply. If nothing arrives by Thursday at noon, I’ll ask again. That deadline doesn’t cancel the trip automatically.

dialogue.speaker: Planner
dialogue.text: The coordinator hasn’t replied. The recorder must be broken.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: That’s possible, but the silence doesn’t prove it. The coordinator might be busy.

dialogue.speaker: Planner
dialogue.text: If we had two confirmed recorders, we’d use both rooms.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: Yes. For now, could Group A move to ten?

dialogue.speaker: Planner
dialogue.text: We don’t know yet. Group B can only come at nine.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: Then ask A before announcing anything. Each participant needs a chair, and either room has enough chairs. The missing information is about equipment and timing, not the number of seats.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Who called Rui?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Ana called Rui.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: And who did Rui call afterwards?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Jo.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Did Jo ask us to publish the interview?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No. She asked us not to publish it before the speakers approved their quotations.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Did Ana say all the names were checked?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No. She told me she had checked the first half and asked me to tell Jo that the rest was incomplete.

dialogue.speaker: Participant
dialogue.text: Has the talk been cancelled?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: No. It has been moved to Room C. It still starts at seven.

dialogue.speaker: Participant
dialogue.text: The notice I saved says Room A.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: That is the older notice. I sent the replacement on Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Participant
dialogue.text: Who should I contact about the route?

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: Our event team. Room C has a step-free entrance, but please ask about any other conditions you need confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Participant
dialogue.text: I’ll forward the updated version and explain that the time hasn’t changed.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: You can come on Friday, can’t you?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: Actually, I can’t.

dialogue.speaker: Kim
dialogue.text: Neither can I.

dialogue.speaker: Jo
dialogue.text: I can come on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: So can I.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Is Saturday agreed by everyone?

dialogue.speaker: Kim
dialogue.text: We haven’t asked everyone yet.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Which headset do you prefer?

dialogue.speaker: Lee
dialogue.text: The black one that works. We can check our own recordings first and then help each other.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Did Lia stop reading when her schedule changed?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: No. She stopped attending the old evening group. She still reads.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: And she stops to make tea?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Yes. That is a pause before reading, not a decision to stop reading.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Why would online meetings be difficult for you?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Because of my connection and my other Tuesday commitment.

dialogue.speaker: Organiser
dialogue.text: Please remember to send your dates.

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: I will. I’m interested in helping, and I look forward to hearing the other members’ preferences.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Had you been checking the captions long when the photograph arrived?

dialogue.speaker: Reader
dialogue.text: For two hours. Six captions had been checked, but we reopened one.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: What will you be doing at ten tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Reader
dialogue.text: Checking the proof with Jo. We expect to have approved it by noon if no new correction is needed.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: So readers can collect the booklets on Friday?

dialogue.speaker: Reader
dialogue.text: No. Friday is the estimated end of printing. Binding comes afterwards.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: And Monday collection?

dialogue.speaker: Reader
dialogue.text: An estimate, not a guarantee. We’ll ask for an update after approval.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: If we had downloaded the file, would the whole event have been perfect?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: We would have had a local copy, but we hadn’t tested the sound. We can’t guarantee the rest.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: What do you wish had happened?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: I wish we had checked both the file and the equipment.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: And what do you wish were different now?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: I wish we had a backup procedure. We still don’t.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Does the missing copy prove someone caused the failure deliberately?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: No. We should discuss responsibilities without inventing intentions.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Can we say Jo changed the time through the personal account at nine?

dialogue.speaker: Administrator
dialogue.text: No. That account could not be used until eleven. But the shared account was available earlier.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Mina denied changing it. Does that settle who made the edit?

dialogue.speaker: Administrator
dialogue.text: No. Her statement is one source, not a complete investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: What did Jo suggest?

dialogue.speaker: Administrator
dialogue.text: Comparing the exports and sending a correction. The team was persuaded to send it, and did so at two.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Is the opening reported to have moved to seven?

dialogue.speaker: Administrator
dialogue.text: Someone has reported that, based on the poster. The booking still says six.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: Could you clarify whether both frames have been repaired?

dialogue.speaker: Technician
dialogue.text: One has been repaired and is being checked. The other is still being repaired.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: And the glass?

dialogue.speaker: Technician
dialogue.text: It is being cleaned. No replacement has been ordered.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: I was wondering whether I could collect both on Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Technician
dialogue.text: We can’t confirm that yet. We’ll update you tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: Understood. We’ve arranged to have the labels corrected by the print shop, not by you.

dialogue.speaker: Technician
dialogue.text: That helps. Please arrange collection only after confirmation.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Can I borrow a camera from the upper shelf?

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: Those cameras are awaiting inspection. They aren’t available yet.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: What about the recorders stored in the blue cabinet?

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: They’re available for a two-day loan.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: If I return one at four thirty, can someone else borrow it immediately?

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: No. We record the return that day, but inspect it the next morning.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: So recording a return is not the same as approving the item?

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: Exactly. Staff carry out the inspection before changing its availability.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Can we say most residents want longer hours?

dialogue.speaker: Researcher
dialogue.text: No. Eight of twelve respondents preferred later closing. We invited twenty registered users.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Did all twenty answer?

dialogue.speaker: Researcher
dialogue.text: No, only twelve did.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: So none of the others supported the idea?

dialogue.speaker: Researcher
dialogue.text: We don’t know. They did not respond.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: Was Tuesday the only invitation day?

dialogue.speaker: Researcher
dialogue.text: No. We sent invitations on Tuesday and Wednesday. Only registered users were invited.

dialogue.speaker: Editor
dialogue.text: And weekends?

dialogue.speaker: Researcher
dialogue.text: None of the respondents was asked about weekend opening.

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: I heard the committee doesn’t support the event.

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: We do support it. What we need is a confirmed indoor room and a completed access check.

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: But Jo sent the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: It was a draft that Jo sent, not the final plan.

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: If the forecast improves, can we announce the venue?

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: Even if it improves, those conditions still apply.

dialogue.speaker: Volunteer
dialogue.text: Has either condition been completed?

dialogue.speaker: Coordinator
dialogue.text: Not yet. Only after both are complete will the committee approve the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Worker
dialogue.text: I used to work evenings. I’m still getting used to the morning shift.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: I’m accustomed to mornings, but I’m not used to this new rota yet.

dialogue.speaker: Worker
dialogue.text: I can attend Wednesday’s briefing.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: So can I.

dialogue.speaker: Worker
dialogue.text: Has the expansion been approved?

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: Yes, it has.

dialogue.speaker: Worker
dialogue.text: Has it started?

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: No, it hasn’t. Approval was on Tuesday; the start is planned for next month.

dialogue.speaker: Worker
dialogue.text: I hope the draft rota stays open for comments until Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: It does. The coordinator’s message confirms that deadline.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: English Club on Friday. At ten, not nine. Room five.

dialogue.speaker: May
dialogue.text: Again, please.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Friday. At ten. Room five.

dialogue.speaker: May
dialogue.text: Friday, at ten, room five?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Yes. Code six, two, one?

dialogue.speaker: May
dialogue.text: No. Six, two, zero.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Six, two, zero. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Maya, are you free tomorrow at two in the afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes. At the library?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: No. At the café. The library is closed tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The café at A?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes. At two, not eleven.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Is Leo going to bring the map?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: No. Please bring the map, Maya. Leo is going to bring water.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I’m going to bring the map. At two, at the café.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes. Don’t take photos inside the café.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Nina, we’ve just confirmed Room B for Sunday, from three to five. The total fee is twenty-five credits.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Have you sent the email yet?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes, I’ve already sent it.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: I haven’t received it yet. I’ll check again. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Nina, my train arrives at two twenty, not two. Can we meet at two thirty?

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Yes. Outside the main entrance. If it rains, we’ll meet at the station café.

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Two thirty, at the entrance. If it rains, at the café.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: That’s right.

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: We’ve matched the titles. Interview A one has been edited, and its speaker has approved that version.

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: What about B two, the other edited interview?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Its speaker hasn’t replied yet.

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: Then the speaker must have refused.

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: We can’t conclude that. They might be busy, or they might not have received the message. We need to check.

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: If we had more approved items, we would include a longer listening session.

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Yes, but for now we can share only A one. We can describe the rest of the work without playing those recordings.

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: Is the opening still at three on Saturday, at the library?

dialogue.speaker: Rui
dialogue.text: Yes. The location changed earlier; the time hasn’t changed.

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.text: I’d rather present a shorter session than treat missing replies as permission.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: My name is Ana. Water, please. Inside, please.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: The lesson is in room three — I mean room four. It starts at half past two in the afternoon, not a quarter past two.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: I usually do the laundry on Saturday, but this week I will do it on Sunday. Jo will look after the plants on Friday. I need to leave at eight. I am in a hurry, but I can still leave on time.

dialogue.speaker: Narrator
dialogue.text: Today is Thursday. I have felt tired since Monday and I have had a headache for two days. I am still recovering from an illness. A follow-up is planned for next week, but the day has not been confirmed. The medical history section has not been filled in.
